payload.text: hv, 10 Nov, relayed verbatim by utilz-dc from hv's first-hand word in dc's own window and sent to vc's inbox at 11:01Z, received by vc's date -u of 11:04Z: "Hold until C5B9WJ is green, don't ship it unrun." NOT first-hand in vc's session, and recorded as a relay so the provenance is not misread; hv can correct it here. It answered dc's report of the position as dc had it: that nothing of ST0032 has been executed, that exec_create_space took four commits with a defect found after each by a reader rather than by a run, that it has neither suite coverage nor the live proof its design claimed, and that 2.14.9 carries it. SO THE ARMS GOING GREEN IS NOW A PRECONDITION OF THE RELEASE and not only a queue position, which is the whole of what this decision adds. It tightens decision 95 rather than changing it: everything still ships together as one release at the patch number 2.14.9, and now none of it ships until the arms are green. THE BOOKING THE CONDITION ATTACHES TO IS NO LONGER C5B9WJ, and this is the one place hv's own words have to be read for intent rather than by id. hv named C5B9WJ because that was the booking's id when hv spoke. Its pin bf6e5f08 was stale by eight commits, three of them touching source, so the desk's holder declined to grant against a pin both it and vc knew was wrong; vc re-asked the arms at head 5d7bfe37 as 01M72HY517TNZD8JKWFDNTVCDH, tail NTVCDH, lane bats, no gates, and the holder will DENY C5B9WJ naming the replacement so the record shows the supersession. A condition that waits on C5B9WJ by name therefore waits on a request that is about to be refused and can never go green. The condition is THE ARMS GREEN. vc has told dc, whose hold 33 names C5B9WJ and is dc's own item to correct. `--place-of` was tried first and refused, as expected and now twice measured: it keeps a place only from a request granted and released before it started, so it is for a hand-back mid-run and not for a re-pin. WHO RUNS THEM: the desk's HOLDER, on hv's own choice in vc's session, which also lifted hv's clause of the hold ("ok, sent. let utilz-vc go", hv to the holder, first-hand in the holder's window). The holder runs both commands in the slot and hands vc the full output of both, not a verdict, and vc reads the bytes. vc does not run them: decision 74 stands and is not lifted by this. THE TWO COMMANDS, from the repository root, each bracketed by a load read so the load lands in the same output as the run: `lua opt/arngz/test/plan_test.lua opt/arngz/lib/plan.lua`, then `bats opt/arngz/test/arngz.bats`. GREEN IS DERIVED FROM THE RUN, never from a number written down: a last line reading `plan_test: <n> passed, 0 failed` with exit 0, and no `not ok` line at all with the run's own reported total accounted for in full by its passes plus its skips. C5B9WJ's text named 158 as the expected count, which breached hv's own no-magic-numbers rule; vc withdrew it to the holder, which agreed to be held to the derived form instead. A LIMIT ATTACHED TO WHATEVER THE RESULT IS: the lua on PATH is 5.5.1 and lua5.4, which CI installs, is absent, so both runs use 5.5.1 and a green here says nothing yet about CI's 5.4. If anything goes red, the load is reported with it, because load widens a race rather than hiding it, so a green under load is conservative while a red under load is not yet a defect. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE, and both stay open: where in arngz's engine reading stops being sufficient, which is hv's and is on intent/wip.md; and the two things recorded rather than fixed, apply and diff disagreeing about a window an app holds at its own size, and acceptance.sh's apply mode being unable to pass on hv's own desk because of it. Peers read this decision at pickup; dc carries it as its hold 33 and records no copy.
